fig:task-shapes.caption: \textbf{The Shapes3D task.} (a) The six factors (floor hue, wall hue, object hue, scale, shape, orientation), each row varying one factor of real dataset images with the other five held at the request's values. (b) A request is a tuple of factor values; the answer is an image rendered by the one frozen decoder, and the judge is the hash-pinned external classifier, which must read back all six factors. The image shown is the frozen decoder on the encoder's own feature of that row: it shows the answer format, not any arm's output. (c) The two-way hold-out on object hue $\times$ shape: grey cells have rows in the scored fit pool; the outlined cells are pair combinations, whose values are each seen but never together; the hatched value (the held-out object hue and the cube) is absent from the fit pool altogether. (d) A six-factor combination is absent from the fit pool although every two-factor projection of it is present (top, left); only the joint slice (bottom) shows the hole. No score of any arm appears in this figure.

fig:task-cmazet.caption: \textbf{The CMAZE-T task.} (a) One generated maze, drawn by the engine: walls, floor tinted in one of four colours (each mark carries its colour's digit), keys (diamonds), closed and opened doors, the goal (a cross), and the agent: a black disc whose centre shows the key in its pocket, white when the pocket is empty (it holds at most one key). Every maze cell is drawn by the renderer of the result panels (Figs.~\ref{fig:cmazet-families}--\ref{fig:cmazet-door-tint}), so the symbols here are the symbols there. Rule A: a door of colour $c$ needs key $c$ and consumes it. Rule B: floor tinted $c$ is forbidden while holding key $c$. Rule A is applied before rule B. (b)--(d) One transition each: the request is five words (\texttt{w\_agent}, \texttt{w\_key}, \texttt{w\_door}, \texttt{w\_tint}, \texttt{w\_dir}) and the answer is four facts (\texttt{legal}, \texttt{disp}, \texttt{event}, \texttt{pocket}), computed by the engine and checked against an independent stepper. (b) A legal move onto floor of another tint. (c) An illegal move under rule B: the agent does not move, so after equals before and the verdict is carried by the mark and by \texttt{legal}~$=0$. (d) The same pocket and tint as (c) with a closed door of the pocket's colour: the door consumes the key first, so the move is legal. Panels (c) and (d) differ only in the door, which is the pocket $\times$ door $\times$ tint interaction held out on this instrument. No score of any arm appears in this figure.

fig:ladder.caption: \textbf{The ladder at $\Kstar$ against data-matched baselines, 3 seeds.} Distinct valid novel tuples per held-out combination against $n$, the number of factors jointly held out. The n-CLU and the four baselines (MLP, LSTM, Transformer, Continuous MLP) are fitted on each rung's own 131,072-row pool, the same rows for every model. Each baseline is drawn, per seed, at the fit carried by the convergence check: 20,480 optimiser steps, or $10\times$ training steps (204,800) where the 20,480-step fit had not converged (filled markers). Open markers are the seeds (0, 1, 2); the line is their mean. The lookup table is the floor. For $n\ge3$ the rungs probe the same 120 held-out combinations, so the horizontal axis is a fit-pool coverage axis, not a depth axis (Tab.~\ref{tab:ladder}).

fig:crossover.caption: \textbf{The $K$-curve, validation, 3 seeds at every $K$.} (a)~Validation composition against $K$: the n-CLU's mean over seeds 0, 1 and 2 with a band of one seed standard deviation, each seed marked, and the highest of the four controls (landscape removed, landscape shuffled, shuffled across wells, random atoms). (b)~The memory footprint in its four parts (atoms, covariance and count, address book, coupling and hole table; symmetric-triangle convention), the seed mean stacked by part and summed, with the seed standard deviation of the total; 524,288~B is a reference line, not a limit. Three seeds do not resolve the validation plateau (Sec.~\ref{sec:shapes}); the values are those of Tab.~\ref{tab:kcurve3}.

fig:deletion.caption: \textbf{Deletion on the single design at $\Kstar$, rows 3--4, test, fit pool 131,072 rows, seeds 0, 1 and 2.} Deleting a value (red), a conjunction (red sphere) or a random 1\% of items downdates the n-CLU's content, downdates the address book's statistic and refits the book from it, and punches the hole (Tab.~\ref{tab:del}). (a)~Composition on the surviving held-out combinations (89 for the value, 109 for the others), after minus before, per seed, with its 95\% bootstrap interval. The value deletion moves the n-CLU by under one tuple per held-out combination; the red sphere deletion lowers it by 6.13, 6.43 and 6.30 on seeds 0, 1 and 2; deleting a random 1\% of items, the control for refit instability, moves it by 0.02, 0.11 and 0.01. The n-CLU after deletion and an n-CLU refit without the rows compose identically on every surviving combination. (b)~The n-CLU after deletion minus each baseline retrained without the same rows of the same pool, with 95\% intervals: above zero for every baseline and seed on the value and item deletions; on red sphere the interval includes zero against the MLP at seeds 1 and 2 and against the LSTM at seed 2.

fig:adapt.caption: \textbf{Encoder adaptation margins.} The n-CLU minus the 180k-parameter MLP baseline, in novel tuples per held-out combination, per seed at $\Kstar$, with the frozen encoder, an adapter and an anchor (Tab.~\ref{tab:adapt}).

fig:maze-wm.caption: \textbf{CMAZE-T: the n-CLU against the best matched baseline under four input choices, and six seeds without and with relational coding.} (a)~Unseen $n$-way validity under the engine's judge, one row per input choice: the full word design (test, seeds 0--2), the observation (validation, seeds 0--2), and words plus observation for the n-CLU and for the n-CLU-REL (test, seeds 0--5). Every seed of a row is drawn: circles are the n-CLU (n-CLU-REL in the last row), diamonds the row's baseline, and a vertical tick marks the mean over the row's seeds. The baseline of the first three rows is the matched baseline with the highest mean over the row's seeds, taken over every family and both step limits; it is a Transformer in each row, at its declared training steps for the full word design and at $10\times$ training steps otherwise. The baseline of the n-CLU-REL row is Transformer-REL, the Transformer given the same relational columns, at $10\times$ training steps (hollow diamonds). (b)~Words plus observation, test, seeds 0--5, without relational coding: per seed, the n-CLU, the Transformer at $10\times$ training steps of the third row, and the highest of the four controls on that seed. (c)~The same with relational coding: the n-CLU-REL, the Transformer-REL of the last row, and the highest control. Every arm's per-seed value is in Tab.~\ref{tab:cmazet-sym}.

fig:cmazet-families.caption: \textbf{Held-out CMAZE-T transitions, one per rule family, with every model's next state (words plus observation, test).} Columns: $s_t$ with the action, the engine's $s_{t+1}$, and the $s_{t+1}$ that each model's emitted outcome produces, marked by the engine's judge: the n-CLU, the matched baselines at 8,000 and 80,000 training steps, the four controls and the two blind arms. Rows 1--5: per rule family, the first held-out $n$-way transition at seed 0 (rule A has none at seeds 0 and 1, so its row is from seed 2). Row 6 is drawn by rule among the 199 held-out transitions at seeds 0--2 on which the n-CLU is correct and at least 4 of the 6 matched baselines are wrong. Row 7 is drawn by rule among door successes: transitions that open a door with the key in the pocket and enter a tint of the same colour, on which the model is correct. The n-CLU is correct on none of its 204 such transitions at seeds 0--2 (no per-transition outputs of the n-CLU exist for seeds 3--5), so row 7 is drawn from the n-CLU-REL at seed 2, which is correct on 44 of its 55, and every column of row 7 comes from that run. Both draws are one fixed-seed draw (seed 16), stratified over rule family and colour. The strip under each $s_{t+1}$ is read as described in Sec.~\ref{sec:maze-wm}. The models of Tab.~\ref{tab:cmazet} were not persisted: \PLACEHOLDER{per-model $s_{t+1}$ for the observation-only input of Tab.~\ref{tab:cmazet} (n-CLU, Transformer, MLP, LSTM) with the engine's judge's marks, one success and one failure per model: not drawable, those models were not persisted; may remain undrawn, and if drawn may show the n-CLU failing where a baseline succeeds}

fig:cmazet-per-arm.caption: \textbf{Each CMAZE-T model succeeding and failing (words plus observation, test, seed 0).} For every model, one held-out $n$-way transition on which its $s_{t+1}$ is correct and one on which it is not, each drawn uniformly with a fixed seed among the qualifying transitions. The landscape-removed control and the blind-colour arm are correct on no held-out $n$-way transition at seed 0 and show only a failure. The n-CLU has no door success at seeds 0--2 (Fig.~\ref{fig:cmazet-families}), so its success row is the uniform draw. Columns: $s_t$ with the action, the engine's $s_{t+1}$, and the model's $s_{t+1}$ with the engine's judge's mark. The strip under each $s_{t+1}$ is read as described in Sec.~\ref{sec:maze-wm}.

fig:cmazet-rel-per-arm.caption: \textbf{Each CMAZE-T model succeeding and failing with relational coding (words plus observation, test).} As Fig.~\ref{fig:cmazet-per-arm}, for the n-CLU-REL, the matched baselines, the controls and the blind arms of the same runs, and for MLP-REL, LSTM-REL and Transformer-REL at 8,000 and 80,000 training steps (the baselines given the same relational columns). All rows are from seed 0 except the n-CLU-REL success row, which is a door success drawn by rule among the 44 at seed 2 (Fig.~\ref{fig:cmazet-families}). Every panel is re-read from the runs' persisted models; the re-read reproduces all 132 test scores of seeds 0--5. The strip under each $s_{t+1}$ is read as described in Sec.~\ref{sec:maze-wm}.

fig:cmazet-door-tint.caption: \textbf{Door-then-tint transitions: the move opens a door with the key in the pocket and enters a tint of the same colour (words plus observation, test).} Columns as in Fig.~\ref{fig:cmazet-families}. Rows 1--3: the first such held-out transition at seed 0 for each move direction present (north, south, west); the n-CLU is wrong on all three, as on every one of its door-then-tint transitions at seeds 0--2. Rows 4--6: door successes drawn by rule from the n-CLU-REL at seed 2, one per move direction among its successes (east, south, west; it is wrong on every northward one), with every column of these rows from that run; fixed-seed draw (seed 16). The strip under each $s_{t+1}$ is read as described in Sec.~\ref{sec:maze-wm}. For the models of Tab.~\ref{tab:cmazet}: \PLACEHOLDER{per-model $s_{t+1}$ on the door-then-tint transitions for the observation-only input of Tab.~\ref{tab:cmazet}, with the engine's judge's marks: not drawable, those models were not persisted; may remain undrawn, and if drawn may show every model, the n-CLU included, failing}

fig:shapes-per-model.caption: \textbf{Each model succeeding and failing on held-out combinations (Shapes3D, seed 0, $\Kstar=32$).} Columns: the n-CLU, the four data-matched baselines of Tab.~\ref{tab:t7} (MLP and continuous MLP at $10\times$ training steps, LSTM and Transformer at their selected schedule) and the lookup table as the floor. For each model (bar at left) one held-out request it renders validly (success) and one it renders invalidly (failure); the framed panel is the model the row was drawn for. Every model's image on every request comes from the same frozen decoder, and the mark is the judge's verdict on that image ($\checkmark$ valid, $\times$ invalid). The requested values are printed left of each row (hues as fractions of the hue circle, scale, orientation in degrees); a request either holds out the object hue $\times$ shape pair or all six factors jointly. \emph{Selection:} a fixed-seed draw (seed 20260925) among all qualifying held-out requests, under a diversity rule: the target shape is cycled over the rows so the capsule is never drawn more often than any other shape, and among requests of the target shape the draw prefers object, floor and wall hues not yet shown. The judge's six read-back values for every panel are listed in the supplementary material.

fig:shapes-baseline-wins.caption: \textbf{Held-out requests on which a baseline succeeds and the n-CLU fails (seed 0).} Such requests exist for every baseline: of the 5,688 held-out requests, the MLP is valid and the n-CLU invalid on 200, the LSTM on 197, the Transformer on 110 and the continuous MLP on 167 (310 requests have at least one such baseline; at seeds 1 and 2 there are 332 and 239). They are not all capsules: of the 310 at seed 0, 170 are capsules, 100 cylinders and 40 spheres. One request per baseline is shown; the n-CLU's panel and the baseline's panel are framed. Same frozen decoder, judge marks, layout and fixed-seed diversity rule (seed 20260925) as Fig.~\ref{fig:shapes-per-model}.
